Overview

This report follows a SystemVerilog two-bit unsigned adder through the open-source TinyTapeout SKY130 flow, from RTL to a precheck-clean GDS layout. Each step gives:

  • what the step does and why it is needed
  • the TinyTapeout constraints that apply
  • the command that runs the tool
  • the verified result
  • what the result means for the next step

Status legend: ✅ verified from the tool’s own output · ⏳ pending.

TinyTapeout requirements used in this report

ID Requirement Type

1. Design and interface mapping ✅

What and why: the adder core computes {carry, sum} = a + b for two unsigned 2-bit operands, giving results 0–6. A wrapper connects the core to TinyTapeout’s standard tile interface, which the chip-level multiplexer expects.

TinyTapeout constraints:

Constraint Requirement How this design meets it
Top module name (R3) must start with tt_um_ and be unique tt_um_tomprusg_adder2
Port list (R3) ui_in[7:0], uo_out[7:0], uio_in[7:0], uio_out[7:0], uio_oe[7:0], ena, clk, rst_n all ports present
Defined outputs (R4) every output bit driven uo_out[7:3], uio_out, uio_oe tied to 0
Bidirectional pins (R4) uio_oe = 0 sets them as inputs all 8 set as inputs, unused
Tile size (R2) tiles in info.yaml 1x1
Clock clock_hz in info.yaml (descriptive) 0: combinational, no clock used
Language Verilog or SystemVerilog accepted SystemVerilog

Pin mapping:

Signal TinyTapeout pin Direction
a[1:0] ui_in[1:0] input
b[1:0] ui_in[3:2] input
sum[1:0] uo_out[1:0] output
carry uo_out[2] output
(unused) ui_in[7:4], uio_in, clk, rst_n, ena not connected
(tied 0) uo_out[7:3], uio_out, uio_oe constant 0

Next: prove the core and the wrapper are functionally correct.

2. RTL simulation ✅

What and why: an exhaustive, self-checking test of the core. All 16 combinations of a and b are applied and each result is compared with a + b. The test fails immediately on any mismatch.

Command:

verilator --binary --timing --trace-vcd --timescale 1ns/1ps -Wall --top-module tb_adder2 adder2.sv tb_adder2.sv

Then run the generated simulator, Vtb_adder2.

Result: 0 Verilator warnings with -Wall; 16/16 correct; PASS: all 16 combinations checked.

Next: repeat the test through the TinyTapeout pins.

3. Wrapper simulation ✅

What and why: the same 16 cases through the wrapper. The test also checks the complete 8-bit output bus and that the bidirectional outputs and enables stay 0.

Command:

verilator --binary --timing --trace-vcd --timescale 1ns/1ps -Wall --top-module tb_tt_adder2 adder2.sv tt_um_tomprusg_adder2.sv tb_tt_adder2.sv

Then run the generated simulator, Vtb_tt_adder2.

Test conditions:

Input Value Reason
ena 1 TinyTapeout sets ena = 1 when the design is selected
rst_n 1 not in reset (unused by this design)
clk 0 not used by a combinational design
ui_in[7:4], uio_in 0 unused inputs; other values not exhaustively tested

Result: 0 warnings; 16/16 correct; all unused outputs 0; PASS: all 16 TinyTapeout wrapper cases checked.

Next: generate the physical-design configuration.

4. TinyTapeout configuration ✅

What and why: TinyTapeout’s support tool reads info.yaml and writes the flow configuration, so that the tile size, pin template, power names and layer limit match the shuttle exactly. It is merged with TinyTapeout’s template settings.

Command:

python tt_tool.py --create-user-config

TinyTapeout constraints written into the configuration:

Setting Value Requirement
DESIGN_NAME tt_um_tomprusg_adder2 R3
DIE_AREA 0 0 161.00 111.52 µm R2
FP_DEF_TEMPLATE 1x1 pin template tt_block_1x1_pg.def R5
VDD_PIN / GND_PIN VPWR / VGND R6
RT_MAX_LAYER met4 R7

TinyTapeout template settings (unchanged):

Setting Value Type Meaning
CLOCK_PERIOD 20 ns default (D1) timing reference, not a requirement
CLOCK_PORT clk default the clock pin of the interface
PL_TARGET_DENSITY_PCT 60 default (D2) how tightly cells are packed
RUN_LINTER 1 template lint the RTL before synthesis
FP_SIZING absolute fixed die size taken from DIE_AREA
Margins (top/bottom/left/right) 1 / 1 / 6 / 6 fixed core inset inside the tile
FP_PDN_VPITCH 38.87 µm fixed power-stripe pitch
FP_PDN_MULTILAYER 0 fixed no power ring, no met5
DESIGN_REPAIR_BUFFER_OUTPUT_PORTS 0 fixed no automatic output buffers
RUN_CTS 1 fixed clock tree step enabled
RUN_KLAYOUT_DRC 0 fixed KLayout DRC is done by the precheck instead
MAGIC_WRITE_LEF_PINONLY 1 fixed LEF abstract shows pins only

Next: run the flow, starting with synthesis.

5. Synthesis ✅

What and why: Yosys converts the RTL into a netlist of real SkyWater standard cells. It uses only the cells’ timing and function models (Liberty files), not their transistors.

Command:

librelane --manual-pdk --pdk-root $PDK_ROOT --pdk sky130A --scl sky130_fd_sc_hd --run-tag full config_merged.json

This single LibreLane command runs the complete flow, steps 5 to 12. A synthesis-only run (--to Yosys.Synthesis) was done first and gave identical cells.

Constraints:

Item Value Requirement
Cell library sky130_fd_sc_hd R1
PDK selection --manual-pdk: use the installed PDK version note
Lint before synthesis Verilator, warnings are errors template (RUN_LINTER)

Lesson learned: the first attempt failed before synthesis, because the shell still had the IHP library selected (sg13g2_stdcell). Passing --scl sky130_fd_sc_hd explicitly prevents this.

Result: lint 0 warnings; 29 cells, 126.37 µm²; 0 flip-flops and 0 latches; Yosys check 0 problems.

Cell Count Function
xor2_1 2 sum0 = a0⊕b0; a1⊕b1
xnor2_1 1 sum1 = c0 ⊕ a1 ⊕ b1 (uses the inverted carry)
nand2_1 2 ¬(a0·b0) = inverted bit-0 carry; ¬(a1·b1)
nor2_1 1 ¬(a1+b1)
o21ai_0 1 carry = a1·b1 + c0·(a1+b1)
buf_2 1 drives uo_out[2]
conb_1 21 constant-0 tie cells for the unused outputs

The mapper prefers inverting CMOS gates (NAND, NOR, OAI), which are a single transistor stage, and absorbs the inversions with the XNOR and the o21ai.

Next: physical implementation in OpenROAD.

6. Floorplan, well taps and endcaps ✅

What and why:

  • Floorplan: OpenROAD sets the die, the core area and the standard-cell rows.
  • Well taps: the sky130 hd cells contain no well contacts, so separate tap cells tie the n-well to VPWR and the substrate to VGND across the whole tile. This prevents latch-up.
  • Endcaps: placed at both ends of every row; they close the wells cleanly at the row boundary.

Constraints:

Item Value Requirement
Die 161.00 × 111.52 µm R2
Die sizing absolute (from DIE_AREA) template
Core margins from the template’s margin settings template
Tap spacing ≤ 13 µm (FP_TAPCELL_DIST) PDK latch-up rule

Result:

Item Value
Die 17,954.7 µm²
Core 155.48 × 106.08 µm = 16,493.3 µm²
Rows 39 rows × 338 sites; one site = 0.46 × 2.72 µm
Utilization 0.77%
Tap cells 225 × tapvpwrvgnd_1
Endcaps 78 × decap_3

Next: power grid and pins.

7. Power grid and pins ✅

What and why: builds the VPWR/VGND power network, then copies TinyTapeout’s fixed pin template. The chip-level wiring connects to these pins, so their positions cannot be chosen by the tool.

Constraints:

Item Value Requirement
Power names VPWR / VGND R6
Power stripes met4, 1.6 µm wide, 38.87 µm pitch template
Power ring / met5 none R7, template
Signal pins 41 met4 pins on the top edge, each 0.3 × 1.0 µm, 2.76 µm pitch R5
Power pins full-height met4 stripes R6

Result:

  • Rails: met1, 0.48 µm wide, on every row boundary.
  • Stripes: 8 met4 stripes (4 VPWR, 4 VGND) at x ≈ 22, 61, 100 and 139 µm, connected to the rails through via stacks.
  • Pins: all 43 pins (41 signal + 2 power) placed from the template.

Next: place the logic cells.

8. Placement and design repair ✅

What and why:

  • Global placement: finds positions that minimize total wire length, while keeping local density at or below 60%. Pins and taps are fixed anchors.
  • Design repair: the resizer then fixes the electrical problems that placement reveals.
  • Detailed placement: snaps every cell onto the legal site grid.

Constraints:

Item Value Type
Target density 60% default (D2)
Placement mode routability-driven, not timing-driven flow default
Input buffers one buffer behind each used input pin flow default
Output buffers not added automatically template (DESIGN_REPAIR_BUFFER_OUTPUT_PORTS = 0)
Max transition / fanout 0.75 ns / 10 PDK flow default

Result:

Change Detail
Input buffers 4 × buf_2 (input1–input4), one per used ui_in pin
Slew repair 2 violations fixed: _05_ and _10_ upsized to _2; 2 wire buffers wire5, wire6 (clkbuf_4) on the long output wires
Tie cells 21 conb_1, each placed under its output pin
Wire length 326.6 → 294.5 µm after detailed placement (−9.8%)
Cells 35 logic, buffer and tie cells (29 + 6)

The logic cluster sits close to the input pins, at the top right of the tile.

Next: clock tree synthesis.

9. Clock tree synthesis ✅ (not needed)

What and why: clock tree synthesis normally builds a balanced buffer tree that delivers the clock to every flip-flop at nearly the same time. This adder has no flip-flops.

Result: the clk net has 0 sinks, so 0 clock buffers were inserted. Post-CTS repair found no setup and no hold violations.

Next: routing.

10. Routing and antenna check ✅

What and why:

  • Global routing: plans which regions and layers each net will use.
  • Detailed routing: draws the real metal and vias, following the sky130 width and spacing rules.
  • Antenna check: makes sure no long wire can collect charge during manufacturing and damage a gate.

Constraints:

Item Value Requirement
Highest routing layer met4 R7
met5 not used R7
Preferred directions met1 horizontal, met2 vertical, met3 horizontal, met4 vertical PDK

Result:

Item Value
Detailed-routing violations 0
Antenna violations 0 nets, 0 pins
Wire length met1 119 µm, met2 52 µm, met3 41 µm, met4 64 µm, met5 0
Vias 161
Disconnected pins 15, 0 critical: the unused inputs (ui_in[7:4], uio_in, clk, rst_n, ena)

Next: signoff timing.

11. Signoff timing ✅

What and why: OpenSTA checks every path of the final post-route netlist. It uses the SkyWater Liberty timing models and the wire resistance and capacitance extracted from the routed layout. The adder has no registers, so the 20 ns clock serves only as a reference: every input-to-output path must fit within the budget below.

Timing constraints:

Constraint Value Type
Reference clock 20 ns on clk default (D1)
Input delay / output delay 4 ns each (20% of the period) flow default
Clock uncertainty 0.25 ns flow default
Timing derate ±5% flow default
Input driver sky130_fd_sc_hd__inv_2 flow default
Output load 33.442 fF PDK flow default
Max transition / max fanout 0.75 ns / 10 PDK flow default
Budget for an input-to-output path ≈ 11.75 ns result of the above
Chip IO pads (context) input ≤ 66 MHz, output ≤ 33 MHz E1

Corners:

Corner Transistors Supply Temperature
ss_100C_1v60 slow 1.60 V 100 °C
tt_025C_1v80 typical 1.80 V 25 °C
ff_n40C_1v95 fast 1.95 V −40 °C

Each corner is analysed with min, nom and max wire parasitics, giving 9 analyses in total.

Result:

Check Worst value Corner Violations
Setup slack +10.35 ns max_ss_100C_1v60 0
Hold slack +7.99 ns min_ff_n40C_1v95 0
Max slew / max capacitance — all 0 / 0
  • Worst path: ui_in[1] → input2 → _08_ (xor2) → _10_ (xnor2) → wire5 → uo_out[1]. It takes 1.40 ns at the slowest corner and about 0.75 ns typical.
  • IR drop: worst case 3.3 µV, which is negligible.
  • Power: about 5.2 µW, with the flow’s default switching-activity assumption, not a measured workload.

Next: final layout and physical verification.

12. GDS, DRC and LVS ✅

What and why:

  • Fill: empty row space is filled with filler and decap cells, so the wells and rails are continuous.
  • GDS: Magic merges the SkyWater cell layouts with the routing into the final GDS, the file that is manufactured.
  • DRC: Magic checks the sky130 geometry rules.
  • LVS: Netgen compares the transistor netlist extracted from the layout with the synthesized netlist.

Constraints:

Item Value Requirement
DRC clean R8
LVS layout matches the netlist flow signoff
KLayout DRC run by the precheck, not inside the flow template
Pin labels not written from DEF, to keep LVS clean (MAGIC_DEF_LABELS = 0) template

Result:

Check Result
Fill cells 1,388
Magic DRC 0 errors
Netgen LVS “Circuits match uniquely”
Antenna passed
Run full flow finished in 1 min 13 s (80/80 stages)

Warnings in this run (none affect the result):

  • Fallback SDC: the flow used its generic timing file; this is the intended TinyTapeout setup.
  • STA library warnings: about SkyWater IO-pad libraries, which this design does not use.
  • IR-drop note: no supply locations were given; this matters only for full-chip integration.
  • KLayout DRC not reported: it is disabled in the flow by the template; the precheck runs it.

13. Gate-level simulation ✅

What and why: runs the wrapper testbench on the final post-route netlist, using the SkyWater cell Verilog models. It proves that the cells added during implementation (buffers, ties, upsized gates) preserve the function. TinyTapeout’s own build also runs a gate-level test with Icarus Verilog.

Command:

iverilog -g2012 -DFUNCTIONAL -DUNIT_DELAY=#1 -s tb_tt_adder2 -o gl.vvp primitives.v sky130_fd_sc_hd.v tt_um_tomprusg_adder2.nl.v tb_tt_adder2.sv
vvp gl.vvp

Result: 16/16 correct; PASS: all 16 TinyTapeout wrapper cases checked.

This simulation checks function only and has zero delay. In the SkyWater models, UNIT_DELAY adds delay only to flip-flops and latches, and this design has none. Timing is covered by step 11.

Next: TinyTapeout’s acceptance checks.

14. TinyTapeout precheck ✅

What and why: TinyTapeout’s own checks on the submission files (GDS, LEF and gate-level netlist). A design must pass them before it is accepted onto a shuttle.

Command:

python precheck.py --gds tt_um_tomprusg_adder2.gds

The --gds argument must be given as an absolute path. With a relative path, the Verilog syntax check fails because its tool cannot mount the folder.

Checks and requirements:

Check What it verifies Requirement Result
Magic DRC full sky130 rule deck R8 ✅
KLayout FEOL transistor-level layers (diffusion, poly, implants, wells) R8 ✅
KLayout BEOL contacts and metal layers R8 ✅
KLayout offgrid all shapes on the manufacturing grid R8 ✅
KLayout pin label / zero area / checks label and shape sanity R8 ✅
Pin check pins identical to the 1x1 template R5 ✅
Boundary check design within 161 × 111.52 µm R2 ✅
Power pin check VPWR / VGND present and correct R6 ✅
Layer check no forbidden layers (met5) R7 ✅
Cell name check valid, non-clashing cell names integration ✅
urpm/nwell check no illegal well/implant combinations R8 ✅
Analog pin check no analog pins in a digital 1x1 tile integration ✅
Verilog syntax check gate-level netlist parses integration ✅

Result: all 15 checks passed. One deviation: the Python KLayout module used for reading layouts is 0.29.12, below the precheck’s pinned 0.30.x. The DRC itself ran on KLayout 0.30.12.

Remaining work ⏳

  1. Official CI tests: adapt the cocotb tests, which still test TinyTapeout’s example design, to this adder, at RTL and gate level.
  2. Datasheet: write the project datasheet (info.md).
  3. Repository hygiene: ignore the Python environment in git, normalize Windows line endings in the source files, and decide which notes belong in the repository.
  4. GitHub build: push to GitHub. The official build hardens with LibreLane 3.0.14 and PDK 8afc8346; that is the final acceptance check.
  5. Shareable export: HTML, then PDF.

Exporting this report

pandoc fabrication-report.md -s --embed-resources --toc -o fabrication-report.html

The HTML file is self-contained, with every image embedded. Open it in Edge or Chrome on Windows and choose Print → Save as PDF.

Every figure is in the assets folder as a separate PNG, ready to paste into slides. They were produced as follows:

  • Waveforms: plotted directly from the simulators’ VCD files.
  • Code and console snippets: rendered from the actual source and log files.
  • OpenROAD and KLayout views: exported with each tool’s own image command.
